tools.description: Creates an undirected graph object that can store nodes and edges with optional attributes. incoming_graph_data: Data to initialize graph, attr: Attributes to add to graph as key=value pairs. >>> G = nx.Graph()

tools.name: compute_degree_centrality
tools.description:
Compute the degree centrality for all nodes in a graph, measuring how connected each node is.
    
    The degree centrality for a node v is the fraction of nodes it is connected to.
    For directed graphs it is the average number of in and out edges per node.
    
    Parameters
    ----------
    graph : object
      A networkx graph
    
    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, float]
       Dictionary of nodes with degree centrality as the value.
    
    Examples
    --------
    >>> import networkx as nx
    >>> G = nx.Graph([(0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 3), (1, 2), (1, 3)])
    >>> compute_degree_centrality(G)
    {'0': 1.0, '1': 1.0, '2': 0.6666666666666666, '3': 0.6666666666666666}
